definitions.gloss: walking or standing with the toes turned in; pigeon-toed
definitions.explanation: A way of standing or walking with the feet turned inward. Also the name of a judo throw.

examples.japanese: {内股|うちまた}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧。
{内股|うちまた}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{筋肉|きんにく}→筋肉：02646_kinniku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伸|の}ばす→伸ばす：01973_nobasu⟧。
⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→自転車：00633_jitensha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{乗|の}ったら→乗る：00511_noru⟧、{内股|うちまた}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{擦|す}れて→擦れる：28852_sureru⟧しまった。
examples.english: After riding the bicycle a long time, my inner thighs got chafed.

examples.japanese: {内股|うちまた}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{内股|うちまた}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{立|た}っている→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: She is standing with her toes turned in.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ころ{内股|うちまた}だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{治|なお}った→治る：19598_naoru⟧。
examples.english: I was pigeon-toed as a child, but it's corrected now.

notes:
Sense 2 is the opposite of {外股|そとまた} and of ⟦{がに股|がにまた}→がに股：33580_ganimata⟧ (bow-legged).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内股|うちまた}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧: to walk pigeon-toed
- {内股|うちまた}⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧: a pigeon-toed walk
- {内股膏薬|うちまたごうやく}: a fence-sitter, someone who takes whichever side suits them (old idiom)
